English: Wooden Mandapa
A simple wooden pavilion, hastily erected by traveling priests to serve as a frontier shrine and gathering space.
Decorated Mandapa
A mandapa adorned with carved pillars and religious motifs, drawing pilgrims and scholars alike.
Stone Mandapa
A more permanent pavilion built from dressed stone, offering better shelter for rituals and knowledge transmission.
Mandapa Hall
A grand open hall, hosting festivals and advanced scriptural learning, constructed with advanced masonry.
Ornate Mandapa
A lavishly decorated mandapa with intricate sculptures and inlaid gems, attracting devotees from distant lands.
Enclosed Mandapa
A fortified and walled mandapa, providing protection to sacred relics and clergy during times of unrest.
Mandapa Pavilion
A sprawling pavilion complex, housing scholars, acolytes, and a library for sacred texts.
Sanctified Mandapa
A sanctified site, blessed by revered ascetics, imbuing the grounds with spiritual potency and learning.
Grand Mandapa
A majestic mandapa with towering pillars, elaborate murals, and a renowned school of theology.
Temple Mandapa
The ultimate sanctum, a legendary mandapa revered across the land for its spiritual authority and scholarly excellence.
